title: Enhanced derived adjunction and monoidal Quillen calculus
statement:
Here a combinatorial differential graded model category means a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded complexes of abelian groups (with cochain differentials and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]), with cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences satisfying two-out-of-three, closure under retracts, and functorial factorizations into (cofibration, trivial fibration) and (trivial cofibration, fibration), with the corresponding lifting properties. The two weak factorization systems are generated by sets. Enrichment satisfies the model compatibility axiom: for a cofibration $i$ and a fibration $p$, the induced map of Hom complexes is a fibration in the projective model structure on complexes of abelian groups, trivial if $i$ or $p$ is trivial. Trivial means also a weak equivalence. Stable means that the enhanced localization has a zero object and finite homotopy limits and colimits, and its homotopy pushout squares are exactly its homotopy pullback squares. A differential graded Quillen adjunction is an enriched adjunction whose left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Its enhanced localization retains derived mapping complexes and all composition homotopies; equivalently one may use the associated stable homotopy theory with its chain enrichment when the model category is stable.

For stable combinatorial differential graded model categories $\mathcal M,\mathcal N$ and a differential graded Quillen adjunction $L:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:R$, the enhanced localizations have derived functors $\mathbf L L$ and $\mathbf R R$ and a natural equivalence of derived mapping complexes
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal N}(\mathbf L L X,Y)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(X,\mathbf R R Y).$$
The unit and counit are enhanced natural transformations satisfying the triangle identities with their coherence homotopies. The equivalence sends $h$ to $\mathbf R R(h)\eta_X$ and has inverse $g\mapsto\epsilon_Y\mathbf L L(g)$. Functorial cofibrant and fibrant replacements present these constructions. Composition of left Quillen functors and composition of right Quillen functors admit coherent derived composition identifications; enriched natural transformations between such functors induce enhanced derived transformations by evaluating on the appropriate replacements. Objectwise weak-equivalence transformations on these replacements induce equivalences. Strict enriched composition, identity and naturality diagrams thereby give coherent diagrams after localization. An enriched functor already preserving weak equivalences has the enhancement induced directly by localization.

The same assertion holds in several variables for an enriched left Quillen bifunctor, meaning a two-variable left adjoint whose pushout product preserves cofibrations and is trivial if either input cofibration is trivial. In particular a closed symmetric monoidal differential graded model category has enhanced derived tensor, internal Hom and tensor-Hom evaluation, with coherent associativity, symmetry and unit maps induced from its monoidal model structure. A closed symmetric monoidal model structure here includes the unit axiom: for a cofibrant replacement $q:Q\mathbf1\to\mathbf1$, both $q\otimes P$ and $P\otimes q$ are weak equivalences for every cofibrant $P$. Enriched strong monoidal left Quillen functors $F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ induce coherent strong monoidal derived functors provided the derived-unit condition holds: $F(Q\mathbf1_{\mathcal M})\xrightarrow{F(q)}F(\mathbf1_{\mathcal M})\cong\mathbf1_{\mathcal N}$ is a weak equivalence. This condition is automatic if $\mathbf1_{\mathcal M}$ is cofibrant, or if $F$ preserves all weak equivalences. For enhanced functors obtained this way, the unit/composition/counit formula defining an adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] defines an enhanced transformation, and mate formation respects coherent composition diagrams. This asserts functoriality for the specified enriched data, not a lifting of arbitrary transformations supplied only on ordinary homotopy categories.

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal M_c$ and $\mathcal N_f$ for the full cofibrant and fibrant subcategories. A lifting problem for $R(p)$ against a cofibration $i$ is, under the given enriched adjunction, the lifting problem for $p$ against $L(i)$. Thus $R$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations: use $L(i)$ trivial when $i$ is trivial for the first assertion, and use arbitrary cofibrations for the second. Also $L$ sends cofibrant objects to cofibrant objects, since it preserves the initial object and cofibrations; dually $R$ sends fibrant objects to fibrant objects.

To check homotopicality on these subcategories use [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations]. For a weak equivalence $f$ between cofibrant objects, write $f=p i$, $p s=1$, with $i,s$ cofibrations and $p$ a trivial fibration. Two-out-of-three makes $i,s$ trivial cofibrations. Hence $L(i),L(s)$ are weak equivalences; $L(p)L(s)=1$ makes $L(p)$ a weak equivalence, and consequently $L(f)$ is one. Dually write $f=p i$, $r i=1$ between fibrant objects. Here $p,r$ are trivial fibrations by two-out-of-three; $R(p),R(r)$ are weak equivalences, so $R(i)$ and then $R(f)$ are weak equivalences.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison] to both model categories. Their cofibrant and fibrant inclusions become enriched localization equivalences. By [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal], localize $L|_{\mathcal M_c}$ and $R|_{\mathcal N_f}$, which preserve weak equivalences by step 1, and precompose with inverses of the respective inclusion equivalences. This constructs $F=\mathbf L L$ and $G=\mathbf R R$ as enhanced functors. Their values are represented by $LQX$ and $RTY$. Functorial replacements supply these objectwise presentations; no enriched replacement functor is being assumed. Inverses of the localized inclusion equivalences give the required coherent replacement comparisons. All categories are interpreted in a larger universe in which the indicated full subcategories and diagram shapes are small. For subsequent uses of derived enriched Yoneda, take the full bifibrant dg presentation supplied by the mapping-comparison node in this larger universe; no general infinity-category rectification is needed.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, enhanced functors and replacement presentations

proof.text:
For $P$ cofibrant in $\mathcal M$ and $I$ fibrant in $\mathcal N$, the original enriched adjunction is an actual isomorphism of complexes
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal N}(LP,I)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal M}(P,RI).$$
Here $LP$ is cofibrant and $RI$ is fibrant by step 1, so [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison] identifies both sides with the corresponding enriched derived mapping objects. Its bifunctor assertion makes both sides homotopical on $\mathcal M_c^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal N_f$. Apply the multivariable and opposite clauses of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] to descend this natural isomorphism. After the inclusion equivalences this is the asserted natural equivalence
$$\Phi_{X,Y}:R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal N}(FX,Y)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(X,GY).$$
This is an equivalence of enhanced bifunctors, not merely an isomorphism on $H^0$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, the finite derived mapping-complex adjunction

proof.text:
Define $\eta_X=\Phi_{X,FX}(1_{FX})$ and $\epsilon_Y=\Phi^{-1}_{GY,Y}(1_{GY})$. Apply [lem-coef-derived-enriched-yoneda] to the bifibrant dg presentations fixed in step 2. Its evaluation equivalence, natural in the representing object and the presheaf, and its coherent-diagram clause give enhanced natural transformations from these evaluations, and its evaluation formula applied to the presentation and to its opposite gives
$$\Phi(h)=G(h)\eta_X,\qquad \Phi^{-1}(g)=\epsilon_YF(g).$$
In particular $\Phi^{-1}\Phi(1_{FX})=1_{FX}$ is $\epsilon_{FX}F(\eta_X)=1_{FX}$, and $\Phi\Phi^{-1}(1_{GY})=1_{GY}$ is $G(\epsilon_Y)\eta_{GY}=1_{GY}$. The homotopies here are the inverse-equivalence homotopies of the enhanced natural equivalence $\Phi$. Since Yoneda identifies mapping objects and their parameter families, the same evaluations on all simplices of that equivalence give their higher compatibilities. These data give the enhanced adjunction, with the specified transpose formulas and coherent triangles. In the replacement presentation they are the adjunction isomorphism of step 3 applied to identities, with the replacement equivalences inserted.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, specified units and counits and their triangles

proof.text: For composable left Quillen functors $L_1,L_2$, each sends cofibrant objects to cofibrant objects. On the common cofibrant domain the composite of the two restricted functors is exactly $(L_2L_1)|_c$. Thus its localization and $\mathbf L(L_2L_1)$ are two extensions of the same functor. [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] supplies their comparison with its specified restriction. For any string of left Quillen functors, every parenthesization restricts to that same strict composite, so the contractible extension space for this entire diagram supplies compatible associativity and identity comparisons in every dimension. The fibrant-domain argument gives the right Quillen version. If $\alpha$ is an enriched transformation between left Quillen functors, localize its restriction to cofibrant inputs; the right version uses fibrant inputs. A componentwise weak equivalence there becomes an equivalence by the final clause of the localization statement. The same restriction argument localizes all the specified strict identity, composition and naturality diagrams. If a functor already preserves all weak equivalences, localize it on the whole source; its restriction to either replacement domain agrees with this construction.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent composition and specified transformations

proof.text:
Let $B:\mathcal M\times\mathcal N\to\mathcal P$ be the specified enriched left Quillen bifunctor. By [lem-coef-dg-bifunctor-cofibrancy-fibrancy], $B(P,Q)$ is cofibrant for cofibrant inputs, each one-variable restriction is left Quillen, and the two enriched right-adjoint families take fibrant $I$ to fibrant objects. The Brown argument of step 1 therefore makes $B|_{c,c}$ preserve weak equivalences separately. By [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison] and [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal], it descends to an enhanced left derived bifunctor, computed by $B(QX,QY)$. For cofibrant $Q$ and fibrant $I$, the enriched adjunction
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal P}(B(P,Q),I)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal M}(P,A(Q,I))$$
and the corresponding formula with $A'(P,I)$ descend in the same way. [lem-coef-derived-enriched-yoneda] identifies the resulting representable presheaves with enhanced right-adjoint families and supplies their parameter homotopies; evaluating identities gives units, counits and evaluation transformations as in step 4. No homotopicality with a noncofibrant fixed input is used.

Apply step 6 to the monoidal tensor. For cofibrant $P,Q$ and fibrant $I$, its closed enriched adjunction is
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P\otimes Q,I)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,[Q,I]).$$
The internal object $[Q,I]$ is fibrant: a lifting problem against a trivial cofibration transposes to one against its tensor with $Q$, which is a trivial cofibration. Thus the mapping comparison of [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison] and the enhanced Yoneda statement [lem-coef-derived-enriched-yoneda] identify $[QY,TY']$ as the derived internal Hom on inputs $Y,Y'$. Its evaluation is the inverse transpose of the identity. Associativity and symmetry are obtained by localizing the given associativity and symmetry maps on cofibrant inputs. Iterated tensor products of such inputs are still cofibrant, by step 6; hence every substituted tensor word and every coherence diagram is homotopical on this same domain. The diagram and substitution clauses of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] give compatible coherent associativity and symmetry maps, including their pentagon and hexagon homotopies.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, closed derived tensor and its evaluation, associativity and symmetry

proof.text:
The enhanced unit is the localization of $\mathbf1$. Choose $q:U=Q\mathbf1\to\mathbf1$. For cofibrant $P$ the maps
$$U\otimes P\xrightarrow{q\otimes1}\mathbf1\otimes P\xrightarrow{\lambda_P}P,\qquad P\otimes U\xrightarrow{1\otimes q}P\otimes\mathbf1\xrightarrow{\rho_P}P$$
are weak equivalences by the model unit axiom. Both sources use cofibrant tensor inputs and compute the required derived tensors, while $U\simeq\mathbf1$ in the localization by [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison]. They give the enhanced left and right unit equivalences. To check their coherence, consider any finite tensor word in cofibrant variables and unit symbols. First replace every unit symbol by $U$, then map any subset of those symbols to $\mathbf1$ by $q$. All resulting operations in the remaining cofibrant variables preserve weak equivalences: strict unitors remove the $\mathbf1$ symbols, and the remaining factors are cofibrant. Every edge replacing a $U$ by $\mathbf1$ is a weak equivalence by the unit axiom with the other tensor factors cofibrant, after removing strict units. For a word consisting solely of units the last such edge is $q$ itself. The cubes of these edges commute by tensor functoriality. Their faces involving rebracketing, symmetry or unit removal commute by the original monoidal axioms and naturality. Localize these whole cubes by [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. Since all the replacement edges become equivalences, their inverses and these specified diagrams supply the unit compatibility homotopies and all higher compatibilities; adjoining another symbol or another edge restricts to the preceding cube. In particular the triangle diagram is the image of the ordinary unit triangle. This treats noncofibrant units without applying Brown to $q$ as a map between cofibrant objects.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, unit axiom and coherent unit comparisons

proof.text:
For an enriched strong monoidal left Quillen functor $H$, tensor comparison on cofibrant $P,Q$ is the given isomorphism $H(P)\otimes H(Q)\cong H(P\otimes Q)$, so [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] localizes it and all associativity and symmetry diagrams. The unit comparison is
$$\mathbf L H(\mathbf1_{\mathcal M})\simeq H(Q\mathbf1_{\mathcal M})\xrightarrow{H(q)}H(\mathbf1_{\mathcal M})\cong\mathbf1_{\mathcal N}.$$
By [lem-coef-dg-monoidal-unit-image], the derived-unit weak equivalence makes every unit-replacement edge in a finite cofibrant tensor word a weak equivalence after applying $H$, and its compatibility diagrams are the localized images of the source unit cubes. Hence the strong monoidal derived functor has the asserted unit coherence under exactly the additional derived-unit condition. If the source unit is cofibrant, $q$ has cofibrant endpoints and step 1 proves the condition; if $H$ preserves every weak equivalence, it preserves $q$ directly.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, strong monoidal coefficient extension; repaired derived-unit hypothesis

proof.text:
Use the directions of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. By [lem-coef-dg-mate-transpose], for an enhanced map $\alpha:L_2G\to HL_1$ its mate is
$$\beta=(R_2H\epsilon_1)(R_2\alpha R_1)(\eta_2GR_1),$$
and its transpose is $(H\epsilon_1)(\alpha R_1)$. Whiskering and composition are available from step 5 and [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. By [lem-coef-dg-mate-pasting], these mate words satisfy both horizontal and composite-adjunction pasting formulas, with the composite units and counits displayed there. The identities hold on all parameter simplices because transposition is an enhanced equivalence, so restriction to faces and degeneracies gives the required coherent homotopies. Thus mate formation respects coherent composition diagrams.
